questions.question: Why must time-series evaluation use forward-moving splits?
options: To balance every period to the same class ratio
To prevent future information from entering training
To remove seasonality from the observations
To increase the number of model parameters
questions.explanation: Each backtest must train only on information that would have existed before the evaluation period.

questions.question: A fraud model has excellent accuracy but misses most fraud cases because fraud is rare. Which evidence should change first?
options: The model file size
The dashboard color
Recall and cost-weighted false negatives at the operating threshold
The number of training epochs alone
questions.explanation: Accuracy hides rare but expensive misses. Recall and explicit error costs expose the production consequence.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a shadow deployment?
options: Replace the baseline for every user immediately
Tune repeatedly on the final holdout
Hide candidate latency from operators
Observe candidate behavior on production inputs without changing decisions
questions.explanation: Shadowing checks compatibility, stability, latency, and output differences without granting user-facing authority.

questions.question: Aggregate quality improves by 4%, but a critical user slice regresses by 3% beyond its guardrail. What should the promotion gate do?
options: Hold or roll back while the slice regression is investigated
Promote because the aggregate score is larger
Delete the slice metric
Increase traffic to make the regression disappear
questions.explanation: A predeclared guardrail is a blocking contract. Aggregate quality cannot cancel a critical-slice regression.

questions.question: Why add guardrail metrics beside a primary quality metric?
options: Guardrails eliminate sampling uncertainty
The primary score can hide safety, fairness, latency, or reliability regressions
More metrics automatically guarantee promotion
Guardrails replace the business objective
questions.explanation: Promotion must satisfy important constraints that the main quality score does not represent.

questions.question: What does repeated tuning on a final test set cause?
options: Automatic calibration
Lower serving latency
The test set influences development and becomes optimistically biased
More independent evidence
questions.explanation: The final holdout stops being independent once its results repeatedly influence model and threshold choices.
